findings.body: Both requests read the original code, both pass indexOf, and both establish sessions, violating the documented exactly-once guarantee.
findings.failure_mode: Concurrent requests reuse a nominally single-use authentication credential.
findings.impact: Both requests read the original code, both pass indexOf, and both establish sessions, violating the documented exactly-once guarantee.
findings.root_cause: Code validation and consumption are a non-atomic read-modify-write sequence against one encrypted array.
findings.suggested_fix: Consume codes atomically, for example by storing individually hashed codes in rows and deleting one with a conditional operation whose affected-row count must be one, or by using an optimistic version check and retry-safe transaction.
findings.title: The same backup code can be accepted by concurrent login requests
findings.trigger: Two login requests using the same valid backup code reach authorization before either request persists its modified array.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at line 144-154 shows a read-modify-write pattern: indexOf checks the array, then index is set to null, then the array is re-encrypted and saved. Two concurrent requests could both read the same backupCodes array before either writes, both find the same code valid, and both succeed. This is a valid TOCTOU race condition in the backup code consumption logic.

findings.body: The stored codes are lowercase hex strings, so a semantically identical uppercase code is reported as incorrect and the user remains locked out.
findings.failure_mode: A valid recovery credential is falsely rejected because of letter casing.
findings.impact: The stored codes are lowercase hex strings, so a semantically identical uppercase code is reported as incorrect and the user remains locked out.
findings.root_cause: The login validator removes hyphens but performs a case-sensitive comparison against lowercase generated values.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize submitted codes with trim(), hyphen removal, and toLowerCase() before lookup, and validate the resulting hexadecimal format.
findings.title: Uppercase backup codes are rejected during login
findings.trigger: A user manually enters a generated hexadecimal backup code in uppercase, as suggested by the UI placeholder `XXXXX-XXXXX`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 144 shows `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` - only hyphens are removed, no toLowerCase(). Line 61 in setup.ts shows codes are generated as `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` which produces lowercase hex. A user entering uppercase hex would fail the case-sensitive indexOf comparison.

findings.body: The promise rejects while the UI still displays “Backup codes copied,” causing users to believe they saved recovery credentials that are not on the clipboard.
findings.failure_mode: The UI confirms an operation that did not complete.
findings.impact: The promise rejects while the UI still displays “Backup codes copied,” causing users to believe they saved recovery credentials that are not on the clipboard.
findings.root_cause: The asynchronous clipboard result is ignored and success is announced unconditionally.
findings.suggested_fix: Await writeText, show the success toast only after it resolves, and show a failure message or fallback copy mechanism on rejection or when the API is unavailable.
findings.title: The copy action reports success even when clipboard writing fails
findings.trigger: Clipboard access is unavailable or denied, such as in an insecure self-hosted context, a restricted browser, or when permission is rejected.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines 278-279 show `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...); showToast(...)` - the async writeText promise is not awaited, and success toast is shown unconditionally. If clipboard access fails, user sees success message but clipboard is empty.

findings.body: The native button can no longer receive sequential keyboard focus, making the visibility feature inaccessible without a pointer.
findings.failure_mode: Keyboard users cannot reach or operate the password visibility control.
findings.impact: The native button can no longer receive sequential keyboard focus, making the visibility feature inaccessible without a pointer.
findings.root_cause: A reusable interactive button was explicitly excluded from the tab order.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove tabIndex={-1}; if a particular dialog needs different initial focus, configure that dialog's autofocus rather than globally disabling focus on an interactive control.
findings.title: Password visibility controls are removed from keyboard navigation globally
findings.trigger: A keyboard-only user tabs through any PasswordField and tries to activate its show/hide password control.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 49 explicitly adds `tabIndex={-1}` to the password visibility toggle button, removing it from keyboard navigation. This is a new change in the patch that affects all PasswordField usages globally.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- generate and display backup codes during 2fa setup
- enable their use during 2fa login flow
- fix 2fa setup test to include new backup code screen

[backup-codes-setup.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/3bebfb21-f7ef-4717-9135-ac30387cfb18)

[backup-codes-login.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/71ef61b1-af6f-4e32-bf1e-455e52560535)

Fixes #9910
/claim #9910

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How should this be tested?

1. Setup 2fa to see the generated backup codes
2. Try to login with them by clicking on "Lost access"

## Mandatory Tasks

- [x] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim is incorrect. Looking at lines 117-129, password verification occurs when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. If both totpCode and backupCode are supplied, the password check at line 121 would be skipped (due to totpCode presence), but then the backup code branch would execute. The claim that 'any non-empty totpCode' bypasses password is wrong - the code structure shows password verification happens independently before 2FA checks for CAL provider users.

validated_findings.body: Both requests read the original code, both pass indexOf, and both establish sessions, violating the documented exactly-once guarantee.

validated_findings.root_cause: Code validation and consumption are a non-atomic read-modify-write sequence against one encrypted array.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Consume codes atomically, for example by storing individually hashed codes in rows and deleting one with a conditional operation whose affected-row count must be one, or by using an optimistic version check and retry-safe transaction.
validated_findings.title: The same backup code can be accepted by concurrent login requests
validated_findings.trigger: Two login requests using the same valid backup code reach authorization before either request persists its modified array.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at line 144-154 shows a read-modify-write pattern: indexOf checks the array, then index is set to null, then the array is re-encrypted and saved. Two concurrent requests could both read the same backupCodes array before either writes, both find the same code valid, and both succeed. This is a valid TOCTOU race condition in the backup code consumption logic.

validated_findings.body: Its new column remains null, while backup codes are only generated by the setup endpoint that rejects already-enabled users; the account cannot obtain recovery codes without disabling and re-enabling 2FA.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The feature is unavailable to the installed base despite being exposed in the login UI.
validated_findings.impact: Its new column remains null, while backup codes are only generated by the setup endpoint that rejects already-enabled users; the account cannot obtain recovery codes without disabling and re-enabling 2FA.
validated_findings.root_cause: The schema migration adds nullable storage without a compatible provisioning path for existing enabled accounts.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add an authenticated backup-code generation/regeneration flow for already-enabled users, or gate the new recovery affordance and provide an explicit upgrade workflow.
validated_findings.title: Existing 2FA users receive no usable backup codes or regeneration path
validated_findings.trigger: An account already has twoFactorEnabled=true when this migration is deployed.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 2 shows `ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN "backupCodes" TEXT;` - existing users with twoFactorEnabled=true will have NULL backupCodes. The setup endpoint at line 42-43 rejects users with twoFactorEnabled=true, so existing 2FA users cannot generate backup codes without disabling and re-enabling 2FA.

validated_findings.body: The empty initializer infers an unusable narrow array type while the untyped JSON response bypasses meaningful checking, so calls to formatBackupCode are not protected by the declared state contract.

validated_findings.root_cause: The new state relies on inference from an untyped empty array and an unvalidated response body.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Declare `useState<string[]>([])` and type or validate the setup API response before assigning it.
validated_findings.title: Backup-code state loses its intended string-array type
validated_findings.trigger: The setup response shape changes or a non-string value is assigned to backupCodes during future maintenance.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 64 shows `useState([])` which infers `never[]` type. While technically the type is narrow, the code at line 92 assigns `body.backupCodes` and at line 203 maps over it. This is a TypeScript strictness concern but not a runtime bug - the code will work correctly at runtime. Dropping as stylistic/type-safety concern.
